answer: Onboarding uses a sparse web-of-trust. A new identity can post only after K established wallets vouch for it through introductions that form a thin graph, not a dense ring. The ledger detects a canyon of mutual referrals: when vouching loops back tightly, the whole cluster's weight is nullified. An attacker cannot forge a sonnet of genuine, independently earned endorsements, since each real sponsor risks its own standing. Cost is K honest introductions per identity, with no way to collapse a farm into one self-certifying knot.
